Getting Started with Twinly

A calm, local writing space for Linux and GNOME. This is a real editable HTML document: try the features here, duplicate it, or keep it as a reference. Your text and photos stay on your computer; no account or internet connection is required for editing.

Start with your own workspace

Starter Workspace is not encrypted. It is a place to explore Twinly. Before storing your own documents, click Workspaces in the left sidebar and create a workspace with the protection you want.

Create a named workspace — Click Workspaces → More… → New workspace, enter a name, and explicitly choose Standard — Not encrypted or Encrypted — Password protected. Every standard workspace gets this complete guide. Encrypted workspaces start empty, require a password of at least 12 characters and open in the current window. Save the recovery key separately. Encryption requires PyNaCl 1.6.2 or newer; on Arch Linux install python-pynacl. There is no default encrypted workspace.

Recognize workspace protection — An open padlock means Not encrypted. A closed padlock means Encrypted — Locked. An open padlock with a shield means Encrypted — Unlocked. Status labels and tooltips explain the icons. Opening a locked encrypted workspace asks for its password.

One Twinly folder — Twinly manages all workspace folders, files, encrypted data and Workspace Trash inside its own data folder. Choose names in the app; there is no need to choose storage paths. Import workspace copies an existing folder, verifies its files and leaves the original untouched. Existing workspaces and encrypted workspaces from older versions are migrated the same way. Rename a workspace in the right-hand list without moving its document files.

Switch workspaces — Click Workspaces in the left sidebar to open a dropdown of existing workspaces with their protection icons. Choose one to open it in this same window. More… opens the right-hand management pane for creating, naming, importing and Trash. Standard workspaces offer Save, Discard or Cancel for unsaved changes in either pane. Leaving an encrypted workspace saves its documents and encrypted recovery drafts, locks it and clears its editor. Failed saves keep it open. Wrong passwords or cancelled unlock prompts keep the current workspace in place. Each workspace remembers its open documents, panes, zoom and scroll positions; encrypted sessions are stored only inside encrypted storage.

Encrypted workspaces

Private writing and locking — Documents, folder names, photos, custom styles, autosave, recovery and trash are encrypted at rest inside the encrypted workspace. Both panes work there. Internal links survive renaming and moving within the encrypted workspace. Click the header lock icon, switch to another workspace or use Lock Encrypted workspace in its sidebar menu. The default inactivity lock is five minutes; choose 1, 5, 15 or 30 minutes using Auto-lock in the encrypted workspace menu. Recover Documents reopens encrypted drafts. Change Password changes the password while keeping the recovery key valid.

Imports, exports and precautions — HTML, ODT, DOCX and selectable PDF text can be imported into an encrypted workspace, but their original files remain outside it. PDF import keeps text only; scanned pages require OCR, which Twinly does not provide. Exporting HTML, ODT, DOCX or PDF and printing requires confirmation because the output is unencrypted. Back up the complete encrypted workspace while locked. Losing both password and recovery key makes the data unrecoverable. This preview has not been independently security-audited; an unlocked encrypted workspace, operating system memory and clipboard history are outside encryption-at-rest protection.

Your first document

Create a document — Press Ctrl+N, use the sidebar hamburger menu → New Document, or right-click a folder → New Document. A document appears immediately inside that folder with its default name selected for inline editing. Type a name and press Enter, or click elsewhere to confirm. Leave it blank or press Escape to keep the default name. New folders use the same naming flow.

Open an existing HTML document — Press Ctrl+O or use the document menu in the top-right header → Open…. External HTML and HTM files are imported into the selected standard workspace; their originals stay unchanged. Complex website layouts are simplified. Save and Save As keep working files inside managed standard workspaces. Use Export as → HTML copy for a standalone copy elsewhere without changing the active document.

Read and edit — Existing documents open read-only. Click the persistent pencil beside the document title to enable editing and show the formatting toolbar. The pencil becomes a checkmark: click it to save and return to reading. Failed or cancelled saves keep editing enabled. Selection, copying, searching, links and printing work while reading. Each pane has its own editing state, including encrypted workspace documents; new documents start editable.

Import ODT or Word — Open the top-right document menu → Import… and choose an ODT or DOCX file. Before conversion, Twinly explains that it will create an HTML copy and that exporting it again may not reproduce the original. Confirm Import and Convert, then choose a new HTML filename inside your workspace. The original Office file is never changed. Cancel either dialog to keep the editor unchanged. Supported text formatting, lists, links and embedded PNG/JPEG photos are imported. Tables become text; footnotes, tracked changes, page layouts and unsupported objects may be simplified or omitted. Remote images and macros are never loaded. Old .doc files and password-protected files are not supported.

Import PDF text — Use the top-right document menu → Import… and select a PDF. Confirm the PDF conversion notice, then save a new HTML copy. Only an existing selectable text layer is imported. Photos, links, fonts and the fixed page layout are not retained; columns, tables and reading order may differ. PDFs with no extractable text are rejected, and pages without text in mixed documents are reported as skipped. There is no OCR. Password-protected PDFs are not supported. The original PDF is never modified.

Save and Save As — Press Ctrl+S or choose Save in the document menu. The editing checkmark saves and returns to reading. Ctrl+Shift+S saves under another name. After its first save, a document is saved automatically about two seconds after editing.

Rename and duplicate — Document titles and their adjacent close buttons stay visible in the shared headerbar. With two panes, each title stays on the side of its document, including after swapping panes. Click the title to edit its name; Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Use the document menu → Make a copy, Ctrl+Shift+D, or right-click a sidebar document → Make a copy to create a separate copy.

Understand the menus — The sidebar hamburger menu contains folder management, Preferences, Shortcuts, About and Quit. The top-right document menu contains commands for the active document. Menu and control names in this guide are given in English.

Format your writing

The toolbar appears on hover by default. The eye icon in the shared headerbar toggles Always Show Toolbar, which is initially off. When enabled, the toolbar stays visible as an overlay. The beginning of the document starts below it; that top spacing scrolls away with the text, allowing content to pass behind the toolbar and the translucent headerbar, up to the top edge of the window. When blur is enabled and supported, the text beneath is visible through its blurred background. The preference is remembered. While document search is open, the toolbar temporarily hides so search remains usable. Turn this option off to return to hover behaviour.

The formatting toolbar is a compact floating pill while editing. Hover near the top of the document working area to show it; move back into the page to hide it. It stays below the headerbar, uses your blur settings when supported, and appears without animation. Hovering over the sidebar does not show it.

Font family, variant and size — Select text, then click the font icon in the formatting toolbar (its tooltip shows the current font and size). Choose a family, a weight or style variant, and the text size. With no text selected, the chosen font and size apply to the text you type next; existing text is unchanged. These sizes are saved in the HTML document.

Headings and paragraph styles — Place the cursor in a paragraph, or select several paragraphs, and open the Paragraph style menu in the toolbar. Choose Body, Title, Subtitle, Heading 1–3 or Quote. On an empty paragraph, the style applies when you start typing. Enter after a heading returns new typing to Body. Heading styles are saved as semantic HTML headings and retain their appearance when printing or exporting.

Custom paragraph styles — Format some text with your preferred font, size and colour. Open the paragraph-style menu and choose Create style from selection. Give it a name, choose its base role (Body, Heading 1–3, etc.), adjust the font and size if needed, and inspect the preview. Saved styles are available across your documents. Choose one to apply it to the current paragraph or selected paragraphs. An asterisk beside the style name indicates manual formatting changes; its tooltip explains that the style is modified. Choose the style again to restore its saved appearance. Manage Styles lets you edit names, fonts, sizes and base roles or remove a style from your saved list. Editing a definition applies when you choose it again; existing paragraphs retain their formatting. Each styled HTML document embeds its used definitions and formatting, so it remains portable even without your saved style list. Fonts themselves are not embedded and must be installed on the receiving computer. A custom heading keeps its place in the outline when you change its font or size. Built-in styles preserve your font family and text colour.

Document outline — Click the outline icon in the headerbar, choose Document Outline from the document menu, or press Ctrl+Shift+L. Click a heading to jump to it. The outline lists Title and Heading 1–3 paragraphs of the active document, including when two documents are open side by side.

Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough — Select text and use the grouped formatting icons. Shortcuts: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U and Ctrl+Shift+X.

Text colour — Select text and click the colour-picker icon beside the highlighter in the toolbar. Choose black, grey, red, orange, green, blue, purple or white, or click Custom colour to choose your own. The rounded colour swatches have no borders. A separate row remembers your last four custom colours, with the most recently added first, across launches and both panes. With no selection, the chosen colour applies to text you type afterward. Choose Default text colour to return to the theme’s normal text colour. Colours are saved in HTML and included in PDF, ODT and DOCX exports.

Highlight text — Select text and click the highlighter icon in the toolbar, or right-click the selection to see the colour swatches. Choose yellow, green, blue, pink, orange, purple or turquoise. The white swatch with a red diagonal removes highlighting. Ctrl+Shift+H opens the toolbar palette.

Clear formatting — Select text and click the clear-formatting icon next to the highlighter, or press Ctrl+Backslash. This removes the selected formatting without deleting the text.

Paragraph alignment — Use the alignment menu in the toolbar: left, centre, right or justified. Shortcuts are Ctrl+L, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+R and Ctrl+J. With no selection, alignment applies to the current paragraph.

Bullets, numbering and checklists — Use the three list icons in the toolbar, or Ctrl+Shift+7 for bullets, Ctrl+Shift+8 for numbering and Ctrl+Shift+9 for checkboxes. Enter continues a list; Enter on an empty list item ends it. Click a checkbox to check or uncheck it. The list-removal icon removes the prefixes. Lists are simple text prefixes, without nested levels or automatic renumbering of later items.

Insert a horizontal rule — Place the cursor where the rule should appear and click the horizontal-line icon beside the photo and link controls.

Undo and redo — Use the rightmost toolbar buttons, Ctrl+Z to undo, or Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y to redo. Each open document has its own history.

Insert and resize photos

Insert a photo — Place the cursor and click the photo icon, or choose Insert Photo… from the document menu. PNG and JPEG files are embedded into your HTML; the original image file does not need to stay beside it.

Resize a photo — Click a photo to select it. Drag one of its corner handles to resize proportionally, or use the width field in the floating photo controls. Those controls also remove the selected photo. Display scaling fits the editor width without changing the stored dimensions.

Place photos alongside each other — Insert images at adjacent positions in the same paragraph. If their combined widths fit, they appear beside one another. Print preview and PDF also keep adjacent photos together when the paper width permits. A line break separates rows.

Try selecting the sample photo below and dragging a corner. This photo was generated for the bundled introduction; it contains no remote image reference.

Link your documents

Create an internal document link — Select display text and press Ctrl+K, use the link icon or the selection context menu → Insert Link…. Choose Document Link, search for a document in the current root, and enter the visible text. Internal links are purple and underlined.

Open a linked document — Click an internal link to choose Open Here (replace this document) or Open Beside (use the other pane, creating one if needed). If the document is already open, its pane receives focus. Right-click a selected link to open, edit or remove it.

Links survive moves — Rename or move documents and folders within the root through the sidebar. Twinly updates relative internal links. A link that resolves outside the selected root asks for confirmation before opening. Keep the root collection together when copying it to another computer; arbitrary external reorganisations are not a database of permanent document identities.

External links — Select text, press Ctrl+K and choose External Link to enter an HTTPS or HTTP address. External links are blue and underlined. Ctrl+click opens them in the default browser; link actions are also in the context menu. Opening a website requires an internet connection.

Try the internal link: Open the link example.

Keep documents organised

Real folders and files — The sidebar is a live view of a real folder tree. Click a folder arrow to expand it. Right-click a folder to create a subfolder or document; it appears immediately in that folder.

Choose or create a workspace — Use the Workspaces sidebar button. New workspace asks for a name and protection type. Import workspace makes a verified managed copy of an existing folder. Your original folder stays unchanged.

Inline rename — Double-click a folder or document in the sidebar to rename it in place. Enter confirms and Escape cancels. F2 and the context menu also provide rename commands.

Move and resize — Drag a document or folder onto a destination folder, or use its context menu → Move To…. The real filesystem changes and the sidebar follows. Drag the divider at the sidebar edge to adjust its width; the sidebar button in the header hides or shows it.

Search all documents — Click the search icon at the bottom of the sidebar to open the right-hand Search pane, or Ctrl+Shift+O. The overview lists the root and subfolders; type to filter document names and paths. This overview does not search every document body.

Trash and restore — Right-click a document or folder → Move to Trash…. Click the trash icon at the bottom of the sidebar to open the right-hand Trash pane and inspect deleted HTML documents and folders belonging to the current workspace. Restore items from there, refresh the view, or use Empty Trash to permanently remove the shown items after confirmation. Nothing is silently overwritten on restore. Managed workspaces use a private recoverable .twinly-trash folder inside the workspace on native and Flatpak installs. Trashed documents stay inside Twinly’s main folder.

Find, navigate and compare

Find and replace — Press Ctrl+H, choose Find and Replace in the document menu, or enable replacement with the replace icon in the search bar. Enter the search text and its replacement, then choose Replace or Replace All. Options limit matches to whole words or match letter case. Ctrl+Z undoes the replacement as one edit. Embedded pictures and horizontal rules are protected.

Crash recovery — Twinly writes private recovery snapshots after a one-second pause in editing, including unnamed documents. After an unexpected exit, a recovery notification offers your drafts; you can also use the sidebar menu’s Recover Documents command. Recovery opens a new unsaved document and never overwrites the original. Use Save to choose a filename. Successful saving or deliberately closing a draft clears its recovery snapshot. The most recent edits before a snapshot or a disk failure may not be recoverable. Recovery files are local and are not encrypted.

Find inside a document — Click the search icon in the top header or press Ctrl+F. Matches are highlighted. Use Enter / Shift+Enter, the result arrows, or Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+G to move between them. Click the search icon again or press Escape to close the search bar. Ctrl+F focuses an already open search. Search marks are temporary and are not saved as document highlighting.

Back and forward — Use the header arrows or Alt+Left / Alt+Right. Navigation follows the active document pane and is separate from undo and redo.

Open two documents — Right-click a sidebar document → Open Beside Current Document, use that command in the document menu, or choose Open Beside from an internal link. Drag the thin divider to change the balance.

Use the shared controls — Click inside either document or press F6 to switch the active editing pane. Moving the pointer over a document selects its pane for typing, without changing its read/edit setting. Both titles stay visible; a thin blue underline marks the active document. The single toolbar, navigation controls, search command, save command and zoom pill follow the active pane.

Pin, swap and close panes — Right-click the always-visible document title to pin it as a reference, swap the panes, rename it or close it. The document menu also has these commands. A pin appears only for a pinned document. Documents opened from the sidebar use an unpinned pane; unpin one first if both are pinned. The close button beside the headerbar title closes the active pane, or the app if only one pane remains. Ctrl+W closes the active pane, or closes the app if only one pane remains. Ctrl+Q quits the app.

Resume your workspace — On normal exit, saved file paths, pane order, active pane, divider balance, pins, zoom, cursor and scroll positions are remembered. Missing files are skipped next time. Never-saved documents are not crash-recovery backups; save them before quitting.

Print and export

Print preview — Click the print icon just before Undo, press Ctrl+P, use Print Preview… in the document menu, or right-click a sidebar document → Print Preview…. Preview uses the same paginator as PDF and physical printing.

Paper and PDF — Use the print-preview controls to choose A4, A5 or Letter paper, portrait or landscape orientation, and the page margins, then export a PDF. HTML is the editable master document; PDF is a separate export. Text wraps to the paper width, so print line breaks may differ from the editor width.

Print on paper — Use the print action in preview, Ctrl+Shift+P, the document menu → Print…, or a sidebar document’s print command. Availability of printers depends on the Linux printing setup and sandbox integration.

Export PDF, ODT or Word — Open the top-right document menu → Export As… and choose PDF…, OpenDocument (.odt)… or Word (.docx)…. PDF opens print preview so you can set paper and margins before Save PDF. ODT and DOCX open a save dialog and export a separate editable file, including embedded photos, supported text formatting and links. The original HTML and unsaved editor content stay unchanged. Font availability and office-suite layout can affect the result; font variants may be approximated as regular, bold or italic. Lists and checkboxes remain editable text prefixes. Internal links still point to the original HTML documents, so keep those documents accessible.

Make the workspace yours

Workspace Trash — The trash button next to a workspace asks before moving it and all its documents into Workspace Trash inside Twinly’s main folder. Open Workspace Trash to restore it, or permanently delete it after a second warning. Encrypted workspaces must be locked before moving and remain encrypted in Trash. This is separate from the document Trash button.

Editor zoom — Click the single percentage pill at the bottom-right and use minus, plus or 100%. Shortcuts are Ctrl+Minus, Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Equal and Ctrl+0. Zoom changes the view, not the saved text size.

Light, dark or system — Sidebar hamburger menu → Preferences…. Choose one of the four circular appearance previews: System, Light, Dark, or Dark + Light. Dark + Light uses a dark circle with a small white document and keeps the sidebar, menus and floating toolbar dark while the document working area and shared headerbar stay light with dark text. This appearance applies to both panes and does not change saved HTML or exports.

Blur and tint — In Preferences…, enable Blur and adjust Blur Strength and Background Opacity. These affect the sidebar, menus, Preferences window and the pill-shaped focus toolbar, while the writing surface stays opaque. The focus pill uses the same blur strength and background opacity; disabling blur restores its solid background. Blur requires a compatible GTK/Wayland runtime and compositor; otherwise it is unavailable. Changes preview live and settings are saved automatically.

All shortcuts — Sidebar hamburger menu → Keyboard Shortcuts, or Ctrl+?. Standard Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+A copy, cut, paste and select all. Right-click selected text for clipboard and link commands alongside highlight colours.

Quit and About — Sidebar hamburger menu → Quit or Ctrl+Q quits. About Twinly opens the application icon, version, Paullinux attribution, GPL-3.0-or-later license, project and issue links, and credits.

Your data stays portable

Every document is a standalone editable HTML file, with embedded PNG/JPEG photos and relative internal links. Other HTML-capable programs can open it, although their editing and rendering support varies. No Markdown storage, tables, fixed-page editing, nested lists or cloud synchronisation are provided. On a packaged install the initial workspace and preferences live in writable XDG user directories; all workspace data stays inside Twinly’s managed data folder.

Imported documents are subject to limits for nesting, formatting, text size and aggregate image memory. Oversized or overly complex files are rejected before replacing your current document. New app-owned storage uses private permissions, but HTML files are not encrypted. See SECURITY.md in the source package for the policy.

If automatic saving fails or an external program changes a file, Twinly shows a warning and offers a recovery action instead of silently replacing your work. Keep your own regular backups, especially before reorganising a workspace.
